Statistical Methods API¶

Advanced Statistical Tests¶

… py:module:: statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests

Advanced statistical helpers used throughout the experimentation toolkit.

The module consolidates non-parametric tests, multiple testing corrections, bootstrap utilities, power analysis helpers, and effect size calculators that show up across the CLI, dashboards, tutorials, and tests. All functions follow the Google docstring convention defined in docs/DOCS_STYLE.md and expose examples that match the usage patterns captured in documentation and notebooks.

… py:class:: NonParametricTests() :module: statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests

Bases: :py:class:object

Non-parametric statistical routines used by dashboards and docs.

… rubric:: Examples

from statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests import ( … NonParametricTests … ) import numpy as np rng = np.random.default_rng(42) control = rng.normal(loc=0.0, scale=1.0, size=400) treatment = rng.normal(loc=0.2, scale=1.1, size=400) result = NonParametricTests.mann_whitney_u(control, treatment) round(result.effect_size, 3) -0.215

… py:method:: NonParametricTests.mann_whitney_u(group1: ~numpy.ndarray, group2: ~numpy.ndarray, alternative: str = ‘two-sided’, confidence_level: float = 0.95) -> ~statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests.TestResult :module: statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests :staticmethod:

  Run a Mann-Whitney U (Wilcoxon rank-sum) test on independent samples.

  :param group1: Baseline sample of shape ``(n1,)``.
  :type group1: np.ndarray
  :param group2: Variant sample of shape ``(n2,)``.
  :type group2: np.ndarray
  :param alternative: `'two-sided'`, `'greater'`, or `'less'`.
  :type alternative: str
  :param confidence_level: Confidence interval coverage in ``(0, 1)``.
  :type confidence_level: float

  :returns: Rank-biserial effect size, p-value, and bootstrap CI.
  :rtype: TestResult

  Side Effects:
      Uses NumPy's global RNG to resample bootstrap replicates. Call
      ``np.random.seed`` or use ``np.random.default_rng`` beforehand to
      obtain deterministic bounds in tests/docs.

  Complexity:
      O(n_bootstrap × (n1 + n2)) time and O(n_bootstrap) memory for the
      bootstrap samples (default 10,000 iterations in this implementation).

  .. rubric:: Examples

  >>> import numpy as np
  >>> from statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests import (
  ...     NonParametricTests
  ... )
  >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
  >>> baseline = rng.normal(0.0, 1.0, 500)
  >>> treatment = rng.normal(0.15, 1.1, 500)
  >>> report = NonParametricTests.mann_whitney_u(baseline, treatment)
  >>> round(report.statistic, 3), round(report.p_value, 4)
  (98224.0, 0.0005)

… py:method:: NonParametricTests.wilcoxon_signed_rank(group1: ~numpy.ndarray, group2: ~numpy.ndarray, alternative: str = ‘two-sided’) -> ~statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests.TestResult :module: statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests :staticmethod:

  Run a Wilcoxon signed-rank test for paired samples.

  :param group1: First group data (paired).
  :type group1: np.ndarray
  :param group2: Second group data (paired).
  :type group2: np.ndarray
  :param alternative: `'two-sided'`, `'greater'`, or `'less'`.
  :type alternative: str

  :returns: Signed-rank statistic, effect size, and CI proxy.
  :rtype: TestResult

… py:class:: MultipleTestingCorrections() :module: statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests

Bases: :py:class:object

Methods for multiple testing corrections used in reporting.

… rubric:: Examples

import numpy as np from statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests import ( … MultipleTestingCorrections … ) pvals = np.array([0.01, 0.03, 0.2]) summary = MultipleTestingCorrections.apply_corrections(pvals, alpha=0.05) list(summary.columns) [‘original_pvalue’, ‘pvalue_bonferroni’, ‘reject_bonferroni’, …]

… py:method:: MultipleTestingCorrections.apply_corrections(p_values: ~numpy.ndarray, alpha: float = 0.05, methods: list[str] | None = None) -> ~pandas.core.frame.DataFrame :module: statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests :staticmethod:

  Apply multiple-testing corrections to an array of p-values.

  :param p_values: Raw p-values to correct (shape ``(n,)``).
  :type p_values: np.ndarray
  :param alpha: Family-wise error rate or FDR target.
  :type alpha: float
  :param methods: Iterable of `statsmodels` method names to
                  evaluate. Defaults to Bonferroni, Holm, Benjamini-Hochberg, and
                  Benjamini-Yekutieli.
  :type methods: list[str] | None

  :returns: One column per correction with decision booleans.
  :rtype: pandas.DataFrame

  .. rubric:: Examples

  >>> import numpy as np
  >>> from statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests import (
  ...     MultipleTestingCorrections
  ... )
  >>> pvals = np.array([0.01, 0.04, 0.20])
  >>> MultipleTestingCorrections.apply_corrections(pvals, alpha=0.05)[
  ...     ['reject_bonferroni', 'reject_fdr_bh']
  ... ].values.tolist()
  [[True, True], [False, False], [False, False]]

… py:method:: MultipleTestingCorrections.false_discovery_rate(p_values: ~numpy.ndarray, alpha: float = 0.05) -> tuple[~numpy.ndarray, ~numpy.ndarray] :module: statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests :staticmethod:

  Apply Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate control.

  :param p_values: Array of unadjusted p-values.
  :type p_values: np.ndarray
  :param alpha: Target false-discovery rate.
  :type alpha: float

  :returns: Reject mask and adjusted p-values.
  :rtype: tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

… py:method:: MultipleTestingCorrections.family_wise_error_rate(p_values: ~numpy.ndarray, alpha: float = 0.05, method: str = ‘holm’) -> tuple[~numpy.ndarray, ~numpy.ndarray] :module: statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests :staticmethod:

  Control the family-wise error rate (FWER).

  :param p_values: Array of unadjusted p-values.
  :type p_values: np.ndarray
  :param alpha: FWER level.
  :type alpha: float
  :param method: `'bonferroni'`, `'holm'`, or `'holm-sidak'`.
  :type method: str

  :returns: Reject mask and adjusted p-values.
  :rtype: tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

… py:class:: BootstrapMethods() :module: statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests

Bases: :py:class:object

Bootstrap methods for confidence intervals and hypothesis testing.

… rubric:: Examples

import numpy as np from statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests import BootstrapMethods rng = np.random.default_rng(123) sample = rng.normal(0.0, 1.0, 1000) _, interval = BootstrapMethods.bootstrap_ci(sample, np.mean) len(interval) 2

… py:method:: BootstrapMethods.bootstrap_ci(data: ~numpy.ndarray, statistic: ~collections.abc.Callable[[~numpy.ndarray], float] = , confidence_level: float = 0.95, n_bootstrap: int = 10000, method: str = ‘percentile’) -> tuple[float, tuple[float, float]] :module: statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests :staticmethod:

  Calculate a bootstrap confidence interval for a statistic.

  :param data: Sample to resample with replacement.
  :type data: np.ndarray
  :param statistic: Statistic function.
  :type statistic: Callable[[np.ndarray], float]
  :param confidence_level: Desired coverage probability.
  :type confidence_level: float
  :param n_bootstrap: Number of bootstrap draws.
  :type n_bootstrap: int
  :param method: `'percentile'`, `'basic'`, or `'bca'`.
  :type method: str

  :returns: Point estimate and CI bounds.
  :rtype: tuple[float, tuple[float, float]]

  :raises ValueError: If ``method`` is unsupported.

  Side Effects:
      Uses NumPy's global RNG via ``np.random.choice``; seed before calling
      to obtain deterministic documentation examples.

import numpy as np from statistical_methods.advanced_statistical_tests import ( … EffectSizeCalculations … ) control = np.array([0, 1, 1, 0, 1]) variant = np.array([1, 1, 1, 0, 1]) round(EffectSizeCalculations.cohens_d(control, variant), 3) -0.408

Power Analysis Simulator¶

… py:module:: statistical_methods.power_analysis_simulations

Advanced power analysis and simulation tools for experiment design.

This module provides comprehensive power analysis simulations for various experimental designs, including adaptive designs, sequential testing, and complex effect structures.
